1. **(P1) Deferred sightings for several types.** `step.ts:344` queues one pending entry per type, and `step.ts:370-379` delivers the first at the boundary, which uses up that snapshot's sighting and puts the second back. So it arrives a whole interval late. **Settled rule:**

2. **(P2) Target preference proven, not sampled.** Sources before caches is checked on one seed at one step. Add a property check: whenever a rumor targets a cache sector, no eligible sealed source of that type existed at that tick; whenever it's a carrier sighting, no eligible source or cache existed. Add scripted cases over at least 20 seeds where both a source and a cache are eligible: every one picks the source.

lines: +The pure rules behind §2's timed reveals, §3's rumors and journal, §5's final-island announcement and §11's comeback leads. `@pirate-sea-race/simulation/intel` has the config, the state, `stepIntel`, `targetedRumorAvailability` and `replayIntel`. `@pirate-sea-race/content/intel` has the constants and the zod validator `validateIntelRules`. The module doesn't import the ledger. It is integer data with no clocks and no `Math.random`, and time is the world tick (20 per second). `objectives-endgame` wires it into `MatchRoom`; nothing calls it yet.
+| Sector grid | 3 × 3, named row by row from "North-West Reach" to "South-East Reach" |
+| Sighting delay | 600 ticks (30 s), equal to the carrier interval |
+| Sector reveal | 24,000 ticks (minute 20) after control start |
+| Carrier reveal | 33,600 ticks (minute 28) after control start |
+| Targeted rumor price | 25 gold (the caller charges it) |
+The validator refuses a zero interval, reveals out of order, a delay that differs from the interval, and names that are missing or repeated.

+`sectorOfTile` cuts the map's columns and rows into three bands each by integer division (`floor(tile × 3 / width)`). Every tile is in exactly one sector, and bands differ by at most one tile. On the 224 × 208 slice sea, the columns start at tiles 0, 75 and 150 and the rows at 0, 70 and 139. `sectorOf(position)` is the sector of the position's tile. A position off the map counts in the nearest edge sector. The config computes all of this from the map size, so the same code serves the slice and the 12-island alpha.

+A rumor names a missing type and a target: an **island**, where a source of that type is still sealed, or a **sector**, where a recovery cache holds one. It never names a rubbing, a player or a position. The generator picks among the eligible targets with the seeded generator (`random.ts`), so the same seed gives the same rumor. It tries three tiers in order:
+1. the islands with a sealed source of the type;
+2. the sectors with a cached copy;
+3. a **carrier sighting**, and only when every copy of the type is carried by someone else.
+Targets already active in the player's journal are skipped, so a player is never given the same lead twice.
+- a **start** rumor for each player at control start, or when a player is first seen after it;
+- a free **fresh** rumor for each type a player lost (§11);
+- a **replacement**, when a journal rumor goes stale.
+Losses and completions come from diffing each player's held types between ticks. A rubbing reserved in a duel still counts as held, so entering a duel is never a loss; only a settled theft is.
+**Journal rumors** (island or sector) are the only leads tracked:
+- A rumor goes **stale** when its target no longer holds its type: the source was collected or the cache claimed by someone else. The player gets `rumor-stale` with the tick and then a replacement.
+- A rumor whose type the holder obtains, by any means, is **resolved** quietly. It gets no replacement.

+**Carrier sightings** are one-shot messages, never tracked, so they can never go stale and can't be used to follow a carrier. At every carrier boundary (control start plus a multiple of 30 s, counted when crossed), the state takes one snapshot of the carried copies: the sector, the type and the internal holder of each. It keeps the latest two. A sighting reads the **older** of the two, so it is 30–60 s old and never the current position. It also skips the requester's own former entries.

+Before minute 28, a player gets at most one sighting per snapshot. A targeted request that hits this cap is answered `capped`. A free trigger (start, fresh or replacement) that hits the cap, or that finds no usable snapshot yet, is **deferred**: it is retried at each later boundary until it is delivered, turns into a journal rumor because a source or cache has become available, or becomes moot because the player obtained the type. A player has at most one pending sighting per type, and deliveries still respect the cap. A free trigger with nothing at all to point at sends `no-lead`.
+**Targeted requests** are `{ requestId, playerId, type }`, and each gets exactly one outcome, whatever the order of the batch:
+- `rumor` or `sighting`: something was delivered. Charge the 25 gold only for these two.
+- `capped`: the player already got a sighting in this snapshot.
+- `none`: nothing to sell. The player holds the type, or the player is unknown, or it is before control start, or no untracked target exists.
+- `duplicate`: the request id was seen before. The step answers it without changing the state or drawing from the generator.
+`targetedRumorAvailability(config, state, view, playerId, type)` gives the same answer without drawing, so the UI can show whether buying would yield anything.
+All reveals fire when their tick is crossed since the last processed tick, so a skipped tick never loses one. Nothing is sent before control start.

+- **First full set:** the first player to hold every type of the preset triggers `final-sector` (the final island's sector) to everyone. Each holder of a full set gets `final-route` with the exact point: the first completer, later completers, and anyone who restores a broken set (with `restored: true`). A player who loses a type gets `final-route-inactive`.
+- **Minute 20:** `sector-reveal` to everyone, listing the sectors with sealed sources and the sectors with caches.
+- **Minute 28, then every 30 s:** `carrier-report` to everyone, listing the (sector, type) pairs of the newest snapshot. Skipping several beats sends one report.

+`stepIntel(config, state, view, requests) → { state, messages, outcomes }` never writes into its input. Each message is `{ to, body }`, where `to` is `{ kind: "player", playerId }`, `{ kind: "players", playerIds }` or `{ kind: "everyone" }`. Broadcasts are `final-sector`, `sector-reveal` and `carrier-report`; every other kind goes to one player.

+Bodies carry sectors, island indexes and names, types, ticks and journal entry numbers. They never carry a player id, a rubbing id, or a source's, cache's or ship's position. The one exact position ever sent is the final island's, in a `final-route` to a full-set holder. The property tests check every message of every run against these rules:
+- five seeded runs with compressed reveal times;
+- one slice run with the real constants for 36,660 ticks;
+- one alpha run with the real constants that skips ticks.
+Their `EXERCISED` check asserts that every message kind, outcome and lead path occurred.
+## Building the world view from the ledger
+On each processed tick, the caller passes `{ tick, players, rubbings }`:

# Match information (intel)

The pure rules behind §2's timed reveals, §3's rumors and journal, §5's final-island announcement and §11's comeback leads. `@pirate-sea-race/simulation/intel` has the config, the state, `stepIntel`, `targetedRumorAvailability` and `replayIntel`. `@pirate-sea-race/content/intel` has the constants and the zod validator `validateIntelRules`. The module doesn't import the ledger. It is integer data with no clocks and no `Math.random`, and time is the world tick (20 per second). `objectives-endgame` wires it into `MatchRoom`; nothing calls it yet.

## Constants (`intelRules`)

| Rule | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Sector grid | 3 × 3, named row by row from "North-West Reach" to "South-East Reach" |
| Sighting delay | 600 ticks (30 s), equal to the carrier interval |
| Carrier interval | 600 ticks (30 s) |
| Sector reveal | 24,000 ticks (minute 20) after control start |
| Carrier reveal | 33,600 ticks (minute 28) after control start |
| Targeted rumor price | 25 gold (the caller charges it) |

The validator refuses a zero interval, reveals out of order, a delay that differs from the interval, and names that are missing or repeated.

## Sectors

`sectorOfTile` cuts the map's columns and rows into three bands each by integer division (`floor(tile × 3 / width)`). Every tile is in exactly one sector, and bands differ by at most one tile. # Task: intel

## Goal

Build the match's information systems as pure, deterministic rules. They tell a player where to go and when the race tightens:
- rumors that point toward a missing rubbing type;
- the journal that marks stale leads and offers replacements;
- coarse, delayed carrier sightings;
- the sea sectors;
- the timed reveals of §2 (the final-island sector when a first full set exists, minute-20 reveals, minute-28 carrier sectors every 30 s).

This information is what turns exploring into a race and brings players into conflict, so it must be useful but never a free tracker. Every output is addressed to specific players (§16). `objectives-endgame` wires it into the match room later. This feature only builds and proves the rules.

## Context

- Read `docs/spec.md` §2 (the phase table and "Time limits and results"), §3 ("Exploration activities": rumors, stale rumors, journal), §5 (first full set: the final route to the eligible player, the broad sector to everyone), §11 ("Preventing runaway leaders": a free fresh rumor on loss, the coarse delayed carrier sighting; the targeted rumor costs 25 gold) and §16 (hidden information).
- Read `docs/architecture.md` and the pure modules this one sits beside and must match in style: `packages/simulation/src/objectives` (the ledger: rubbing locations, `freshRumors`) and `packages/simulation/src/claim` (the step shape and seeded property tests), plus `packages/content/src/seaMap.ts` (map size, islands) and `tests/unit/purity.test.ts`.
- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration` and `npm run build`.
- Other features run at the same time and own the sea, server, web, tests, the duel and `packages/*/src/ruins`. Stay inside your owned paths.
- **This machine is shared by several runs. Never stop processes by name pattern (`pkill -f`, `killall`, and so on). Stop only the PIDs you started.**

## Constraints

- Owned paths only: `packages/simulation/src/intel`, `packages/content/src/intel`, `docs/intel.md`, and `packages/simulation/package.json` and `packages/content/package.json` **only to add one subpath export each** (`@pirate-sea-race/simulation/intel`, `@pirate-sea-race/content/intel`, following the existing pattern with the `@pirate-sea-race/source` condition first). Do not change their `postbuild` scripts, dependencies, any existing source file, barrel, tsconfig or root file.
- Independent of the ledger's code: the caller passes a per-tick **world view** (for each rubbing, its type and where it is: a sealed source with its island, a cache position, a carrier with position, or reserved in a duel; each player's held types and position; which islands are claimed out). Don't import `objectives`, so the two stay decoupled. Gold for bought rumors is the caller's (ledger) business; this module only generates the rumor.
- Pure and integer: no Phaser, Colyseus, DOM, timers, wall-clock time, `Math.random` or floating-point transcendental functions. Time is the world tick (20 per second). Randomness comes from the seeded generator (`random.ts`). Durations are named content constants in seconds, converted to ticks.
- The step shape: `stepIntel(config, state, worldView, requests) → { state, messages, outcomes }`. Every message names its recipients: one player, several, or everyone. It never mutates its input.
- **Targeted rumor requests** are `{ requestId, playerId, type }`. Each gets exactly one outcome, `{ requestId, result: "rumor" | "sighting" | "capped" | "none" | "duplicate" }`, so the caller charges 25 gold only for `rumor` or `sighting`. A repeated `requestId` is answered `duplicate` without changing the state or using the generator. An exported pure `targetedRumorAvailability(config, state, worldView, playerId, type)` lets the UI show whether buying would yield anything.

## Design (settled)

- **Sectors.** The map is divided into a 3 × 3 grid of named sectors (for example "North-West Reach", "Central Waters"), computed from the map size in the config. `sectorOf(position)` is total and deterministic on the boundaries.
- **Rumors.** A rumor names a missing type and a target: an **island** (a sealed source of that type there) or a **sector** (a cache or a carrier). It never names a rubbing id or an exact position. Generation picks, deterministically from the seed, among the eligible targets for a type the player lacks. It prefers sealed sources, then caches, then a carrier sighting. It never picks a target that is the player's own inventory. Rumors are made in four cases:
  - a **starting rumor** for each player at control start (§2);
  - a **fresh rumor** when the world view shows a type was stolen from the player (§11);
  - a **targeted rumor** on request, gold-gated by the caller (§11);
  - a **replacement lead** from the journal.
- **Two kinds of lead.**
  - **Journal rumors** target only islands (sealed sources) or cache sectors. Only these go stale: when the target no longer holds a copy of that type, the rumor is marked stale (a message to its holder, with the tick), and the journal offers a replacement from the remaining sources and caches.
  - A **carrier sighting** is a one-shot message: the sector where a carrier of that type was 30 s earlier, never the current one. It is **never** tracked for staleness, so carrier movement can't leak live information. It is sent only on three triggers: a fresh rumor after a loss when every other copy is carried, a targeted rumor under the same condition, or a journal replacement when every remaining copy is carried. At most one carrier sighting per player per carrier interval (30 s) before minute 28.
  - A rumor whose type its holder has since obtained is retired quietly (a "resolved" message, no replacement).
- **Carrier snapshots (not a rolling history).** At each 30 s carrier boundary counted from control start (crossing-based), the state takes one snapshot: the sector, type and internal holder of each carried copy. It keeps only the latest two. A carrier sighting reads the **older** snapshot, so it is 30–60 s old and never the current location, by construction. The minute-28 broadcast reads the newer one. Snapshot entries held by the requester themselves are never used for that requester's sighting.
- **The sighting cap** lines up with the snapshots: at most one sighting per player per snapshot, before minute 28. A **free** trigger (a fresh rumor after a loss, or a journal replacement) that hits the cap is **deferred**, not dropped: it is delivered at the next snapshot boundary (at most one pending per player).

- **What sightings and broadcasts contain:** a sector and a rubbing type, never a player id, a rubbing id or an exact position.
- **Losses and completions come from diffing** each player's held types between ticks. The ledger's sticky `freshRumors` flag isn't used as a signal.
- **Robust to skipped ticks:** reveals and intervals fire when a boundary is crossed since the last processed tick (`>=`), not on equality, so a skipped or batched tick never loses one.
- **Timed reveals** (§2), counted from control start (`controlStartTick` in the config):
  - **The first full set:** when a player first holds all the preset's types, everyone gets the final island's sector, and that player gets the exact final-island position (their "route"). If they lose a type, their route becomes inactive until the set is restored. A later completer gets their own route message. The final island's position comes from the config.
  - **Minute 20:** everyone gets the sectors that contain unclaimed rubbings (sealed sources) and abandoned caches.
  - **Minute 28 on:** every 30 s, everyone gets the approximate sectors of rubbing carriers.
  - **Minute 35:** nothing here; the claim code ends the match.
- **Hidden information.** No message to a player contains another player's exact position, a rubbing id or a source's exact location. The only exact position ever sent is the final island's, and only to a complete-set player. A test asserts this over every message of every property run.

Each item names the test that proves it. Tests live in `packages/simulation/src/intel` unless noted.

1. **Sectors:** every map cell maps to exactly one of nine sectors; the boundaries are deterministic; the names are unique.
2. **Rumors:** scripted tests for each of the four cases:
   - targets prefer sources, then caches, then carriers;
   - there is never a rumor for a type the player holds, and never one pointing at the player's own inventory;
   - the same seed gives the same rumor.
3. **Staleness and the journal:** scripted tests:

   - a capped free trigger is delivered at the next boundary;

4. **Reveals:** scripted tests at the exact boundary ticks:
   - the first full set, including a lost-then-restored set and a second completer;

   - minute 28, then every 30 s;

   - no player gets more than one carrier sighting per snapshot before minute 28;
   - no stale message is ever sent for a carrier sighting;

## Goal

Build the match's information systems as pure, deterministic rules. They tell a player where to go and when the race tightens:
- rumors that point toward a missing rubbing type;
- the journal that marks stale leads and offers replacements;
- coarse, delayed carrier sightings;
- the sea sectors;
- the timed reveals of §2 (the final-island sector when a first full set exists, minute-20 reveals, minute-28 carrier sectors every 30 s).

This information is what turns exploring into a race and brings players into conflict, so it must be useful but never a free tracker. Every output is addressed to specific players (§16). `objectives-endgame` wires it into the match room later. This feature only builds and proves the rules.

## Context

- Read `docs/spec.md` §2 (the phase table and "Time limits and results"), §3 ("Exploration activities": rumors, stale rumors, journal), §5 (first full set: the final route to the eligible player, the broad sector to everyone), §11 ("Preventing runaway leaders": a free fresh rumor on loss, the coarse delayed carrier sighting; the targeted rumor costs 25 gold) and §16 (hidden information).

- **Rumors.** A rumor names a missing type and a target: an **island** (a sealed source of that type there) or a **sector** (a cache or a carrier). It never names a rubbing id or an exact position. Generation picks, deterministically from the seed, among the eligible targets for a type the player lacks. It prefers sealed sources, then caches, then a carrier sighting. It never picks a target that is the player's own inventory. Rumors are made in four cases:
  - a **starting rumor** for each player at control start (§2);
  - a **fresh rumor** when the world view shows a type was stolen from the player (§11);
  - a **targeted rumor** on request, gold-gated by the caller (§11);
  - a **replacement lead** from the journal.
- **Two kinds of lead.**
  - **Journal rumors** target only islands (sealed sources) or cache sectors. Only these go stale: when the target no longer holds a copy of that type, the rumor is marked stale (a message to its holder, with the tick), and the journal offers a replacement from the remaining sources and caches.

At most one carrier sighting per player per carrier interval (30 s) before minute 28.

  - **Minute 28 on:** every 30 s, everyone gets the approximate sectors of rubbing carriers.
  - **Minute 35:** nothing here; the claim code ends the match.

Both findings are fixed and all four required checks pass after a fresh `npm ci`. Nothing is committed, per the workflow rules; the controller and reviewers still decide acceptance.

**Restoring the snapshot:** the restore from `9c1861e` (excluding `features/`) worked, and the check against the snapshot printed nothing. Every restored path is inside the owned paths.

**Finding 1 (two lost types arriving an interval apart)**
- **How it works now:** each player has at most one pending sighting message, which holds a set of types. Any capped free trigger adds its type to that set.
- **At the next boundary:** every pending type still eligible goes out together in one message. A type with a new source or cache gets a journal rumor instead. A type the player got back is dropped. A type with no copy left sends `no-lead`.
- **The cap:** one sighting message per player per snapshot before minute 28.
- **Message shape change:** a carrier-sighting message now carries a list, one entry per type (type, reason, sector, name), all from the same older snapshot. The old single `type`/`reason`/`sector`/`name` fields are gone. Nothing outside this feature reads the message yet, but `objectives-endgame` will have to use the new shape.
- **Tests:**
  - A scripted test where two types are delivered together at the next boundary.
  - A scripted test where a third capped trigger joins the set and all three go out in one message.
  - The property checker now verifies after every step that each player has at most one pending message with no repeated types. It also verifies that each deferred type is delivered at the first boundary after it was capped. If it wasn't, the checker confirms the type became ineligible, or that the older snapshot showed no other carrier of it (in which case it must still be pending).
- The existing scripted tests only changed to the new message and pending shape; their scenarios and values are the same.
- `docs/intel.md` now states the settled rule.

**Finding 2 (sources before caches):**
- The property checker now tests every rumor: a cache lead only when no sealed source of that type exists outside the player's open journal entries, and a carrier sighting only when no source or cache of the type exists.
- A new scripted test covers 24 seeds where both a source and a cache are eligible. Start, bought and fresh rumors always pick a source.

**Proof the tests catch the bugs:** I briefly put each bug back by hand, then reverted it.
- Delivering only the first pending type made both new scripted tests and the alpha property run fail.
- Letting caches compete with sources made both scripted preference tests and two property runs fail.

- Each type in a sighting message carries the reason of the trigger that asked for it, since one merged message can mix triggers.
